memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Moses had granted the two and a half tribes their inheritance east of the Jordan but had not granted the Levites an inheritance among the rest, for the Levites received no share of the land but only towns to live in, with pasturelands for their flocks and herds. So the Israelites divided the land, just as the Lord had commanded Moses - Josh 14:3-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once again the writer pauses to note the Levites. While the other tribes received full territories, the Levites were given only towns to live in and pasture for their animals. No sweeping inheritance of land. It would be easy to read this as the Levites drawing the short straw — but Scripture has already told us the deeper truth: the Lord Himself was their inheritance.

The phrase that closes this section is quietly important: "just as the Lord had commanded Moses." Everything was done in obedience to God's earlier word. Israel was not inventing its own arrangement; it was carefully following what God had already spoken. Faithfulness here looks like doing exactly what God said, even in the practical business of dividing land.

There is a gentle challenge in the Levites' example for us. Their calling was to serve God and live scattered among the tribes, without the security of their own territory. They had to trust God for their provision in a way the other tribes did not. Yet they were not poorer for it — they were nearer to God. In Christ, all of us are now called to hold earthly security loosely, trusting our Father to provide, and to treasure nearness to Him above possessions (Matt 6:33). The Levites lived by trust, and so are we invited to live.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where are you tempted to grasp for security instead of trusting God to provide?
- What might it mean to treasure nearness to God above possessions?
- How does careful obedience to God's word shape your daily decisions?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, teach me to hold earthly security loosely and to trust You for my provision. Help me to treasure nearness to You above every possession. Amen.
